# Guided Review

> A better way for humans to review AI-generated code. Chrome extension that clusters GitHub PR diffs into ordered review units with short summaries — free, open source, bring your own LLM key.

Guided Review is a Chrome extension for github.com pull requests. AI structures the walkthrough; humans still decide. It never auto-approves PRs, never “reviews for you,” and has no product backend: traffic goes only to GitHub and the user’s AI provider.

---

## What it does

On a GitHub PR page, Guided Review adds a **Start Guided Review** button. When you start a review, the extension:

1. Reads the PR’s unified diff (fetched in the background service worker)
2. Sends that diff to **your** configured AI provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, or Grok) with your own API key
3. Turns the response into a sequence of **review units** — logical groups of hunks with short commentary
4. Shows those units in a Shadow DOM overlay so you step through the change set in a sensible order (schema, logic, call-sites, tests — not alphabetical files)

You stay on GitHub. The model plans structure and commentary only; the code you see always comes from the real parsed diff. Without an API key you still get the overlay and a file-by-file plan — no AI clustering or summaries.

### Core ideas

- **Review units, not file lists** — Related hunks are clustered so you read the change, not the alphabetical tree
- **Keyboard-first** — Navigate units, search the diff, comment, and submit without leaving the keys
- **Short summaries** — Optional two-line overviews per unit; take them with a grain of salt
- **BYO key** — Claude, OpenAI, or Grok; keys stay in `chrome.storage.local`
- **Open source** — Apache-2.0; fork, audit, or point at another provider

### What it does not do

- Does not auto-approve or reject pull requests
- Does not replace human judgment or “taste”
- Does not run a Guided Review backend for review data — no SaaS product API for diffs or keys
- Does not work outside `https://github.com/*` (no GitHub Enterprise custom hosts or other forges yet)

---

## How a review plan works

Pipeline (high level):

1. **diffParser** — Parse the real unified diff into files and hunks
2. **buildPrompt** — Chunk large PRs by file (never splits a single file); ~60k characters per chunk
3. **Provider stream** — User’s Anthropic / OpenAI / Grok client streams a plan
4. **streamPlanParser / reviewPlan** — Validate structure; drop bad hunk ids
5. **Overlay** — Render units from the real diff + plan commentary

Sessions live in `chrome.storage.session`, keyed by `owner/repo#number`. Optional GitHub device OAuth is only required to submit reviews and line comments from the overlay — not to generate or walk a plan.

Cost: one annotate call per diff chunk when a provider is configured. Walking units, searching, drafting comments, and submitting to GitHub do not call the model again.

---

## Getting started

1. Install the extension (Chrome Web Store or load unpacked from source)
2. Open options and configure an AI provider + API key
3. Open any github.com pull request and click **Start Guided Review**
4. Step through units; optionally draft line comments and submit Comment / Approve / Request Changes

---

## Privacy model

- **Extension product paths** talk only to GitHub and the user’s AI provider. There is no Guided Review backend for diffs, keys, or review traffic.
- **API keys and settings** stay in `chrome.storage.local` on the user’s machine.
- **Active session** (diff, plan, step index) lives in `chrome.storage.session` until the browser session ends.
- **Draft comments** stay local until the user explicitly submits a review.
- **Marketing site** may use analytics for page views and CTA clicks; the extension does not embed product analytics.

Details: [Privacy & data](https://guidedreview.dev/docs/privacy-and-data) · [Privacy Policy](https://guidedreview.dev/privacy)
